answers.text: The type of diuretic that would be used in cases of intracranial hypertension from head injury or glaucoma would be one of the osmotic diuretics such as mannitol.

Most osmotic diuretics need to be injected, and once in the system, they directly pull fluid from interstitial spaces. This differs from other diuretics that mainly excrete fluid in the urine, and then the decreased fluids in the blood allow the fluid in congested areas to slowly normalise.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: No, this statement is false, as the osmotic diuretics are actually a weaker diuretic in themselves, so they actually reduce fluid volume less than most other diuretics. But they have the direct effect of increasing osmolarity of the blood, thus being valuable in intracranial hypertension and glaucoma.
